source.note: Search summary (results: parkcitymountain.com "Mountain Stats, Elevation & Snowfall" page, Visit Park City): 7,300 acres, 41 lifts, two base areas (Mountain Village and Canyons Village). character: One of the largest ski areas in the US, created when Vail Resorts linked the Park City and Canyons ski areas for the 2015-16 season. It has two main bases, Park City Mountain Village and Canyons Village, plus a Town Lift from historic Main Street, and it is ticketed separately from neighbouring Deer Valley.
learning: Reference note: beginner areas exist at both bases (the First Time lift area at Park City Mountain Village and learning terrain at Canyons Village), and lessons run through the resort ski and ride school. Confirm current learning lifts and lesson products.

Search summary: 2025-26 opening Dec. 5, 2025 (Ski Utah 2025-26 opening-dates list). Mountain Village closed for the season in March 2026 (TownLift: https://townlift.com/2026/03/park-city-mountain-pulls-the-plug-on-mountain-village-this-weekend/) while the Canyons Village closing was still "TBD", so no single closing date is recorded.

season.notes: 2026-27: planned opening Nov. 20, 2026 (Vail Resorts release; search summary 2026-09-30). No 2026-27 closing date was found. In 2025-26 the Mountain Village side closed in March 2026 while the Canyons Village closing was still to be decided.

prices.note: 2026-27 peak-day adult ticket $369 — "better understood as the ceiling for a peak ski day"; Park City prices dynamically and advance/non-peak dates are cheaper (not captured). 2025-26 peak was about $354 after fees.

source.note: TownLift (Sep 4, 2026, read 2026-10-03): "For the 2026-27 season, a peak-day adult lift ticket at Park City Mountain will cost $369".
